statement: For a finite graph consisting of two disjoint chamber graphs joined only by a k-edge simple corridor with degree-two interior vertices, independent Bernoulli(p) bonds give P(S connects T)=p^k P_L(S connects u) P_R(v connects T)<=p^k, for terminals S in the left chamber and T in the right. The bound is sharp when S={u} and T={v}.
assumptions: No other inter-chamber edges or external identifications
Mutually disjoint chamber and corridor edge families with product bond measure
proof_or_counterexample: Every corridor edge is a separating bridge. A crossing is exactly the intersection of the two chamber connection events and the event that all k corridor edges are open; the three events use disjoint independent edge families.
remaining_gap: No gap in this author proof of the stated finite-graph case; independent audit pending. Does not identify any C0017 scaling limit.

statement: There are bounded Jordan domains D_n contained in the unit square Q with fixed distinct corner marks, closure and boundary Hausdorff convergence to Q, area convergence, and unmarked Caratheodory kernel Q, whose induced mesh-1/n critical square-lattice left-right crossing probabilities are at most 2^{-(floor(sqrt(n))+1)} and tend to zero. Define t=floor(sqrt(n)), a=t, b=2t+1, m=floor(n/2); D_n is the interior of the union of [0,a/n]x[0,1], [b/n,1]x[0,1], and [a/n,b/n]x[(m-1/2)/n,(m+1/2)/n], n>=81.
assumptions: Induced nearest-neighbor graph on mesh vertices in the closure of D_n
Source x=0 and sink x=1; free graph connectivity
proof_or_counterexample: Only the y=m/n row crosses the removed band, giving k=b-a=t+1 mandatory independent bonds. Lemma 1 bounds crossing. Removed geometry is confined to x<=b/n; every compact subset of Q eventually lies in the right chamber. Explicit bounds are closure distance <=k/(2n), boundary distance <=b/n, area loss k(n-1)/n^2, and t*n removed vertices.
remaining_gap: Uses a deliberately overstrong unmarked approximation bridge; does not refute properly marked C0017. Positive canonical-square lower bound uses classical RSW, whose citation is being checked.

statement: For the D_n of L2 and normalized Riemann maps f_n from the unit disk with f_n(0)=(1/2,1/2), f_n'(0)>0, the preimages of A=(0,1) and B=(0,0) have chord distance at most 8/n. Thus fixed distinct Euclidean marks fail to converge as distinct marked prime ends of the limiting square.
assumptions: Brownian harmonic measure and its conformal invariance
The only passage from the right chamber to the left is the gate of height 1/n at x=b/n
proof_or_counterexample: The boundary arc containing both A and B lies behind the gate. Brownian motion from the basepoint must first hit the gate; the half-plane Poisson kernel bounds this probability by 1/[pi*n*(1/2-b/n)]<=4/(pi*n). Its conformal preimage has angle <=8/n and contains both marked preimages.
remaining_gap: Independent audit of the gate-event comparison and normalization pending. The legitimate C0017 law-identification gap remains open in this packet.
